stem: Energy consumed in a home is 250 units then the total energy in Joules will be:
expl: Electricity consumption is measured in “units”. 1 unit = 1 kilowatt-hour (1 kWh) 1 kWh = 1000 joule/sec × 3600 seconds = 3,600,000 joule = 3.6 × 106 joule The Totale energy Consumed from 250 units of energy will be-Total energy = 250 × 3.6 × 106 joule = 900 × 106 joule = 9 × 108 joule

stem: The temperature point at which the solid, liquid and gaseous states may stay together is known as

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / more than one of the above

expl: The fixed temperature and pressure at which a substance remains in equilibrium in all three states (solid, liquid, and gas) at the same time is called the triple point. Example: Triple point of water—Temperature = 0.01°C and pressure = 611 Pa

stem: The boiling point of liquids at higher altitudes -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: When pressure increases, the boiling point of a liquid increases, and when pressure decreases, the boiling point decreases. Pressure and boiling point are directly proportional. Therefore, the boiling point decreases with altitude because atmospheric pressure decreases with height.

stem: Water is an excellent cooling agent because of its

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Water is an excellent cooling agent because of its high specific heat. This means a large amount of heat is required to raise its temperature, and similarly a large amount of heat must be removed to cool it. Therefore, water does not heat up quickly and does not cool down quickly, which makes it a good cooling agent.

stem: A Room can be cooling is done by –
expl: When a compressed gas is released, the temperature decreases and the room becomes cool. In an air conditioner, a compressed gas is used.

stem: The poorest conductor of heat among the following is :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above / More than one of the above

expl: Any substance through which heat does not flow is called a poor conductor (insulator); e.g., wood, glass, etc. All metals are good conductors of heat, but compared to other metals, lead and mercury have relatively low (poor) thermal conductivity. The thermal conductivity of lead is about 34.7 W/ mK, whereas the thermal conductivity of mercury is about 8.3 W/mK.

stem: Compared to a burn due to air at 100°C, the burn due to steam at 100°C is

options.label: a
options.text: Less dangerous due to high latent heat of evaporation

options.label: b
options.text: More dangerous due to high latent heat of evaporation

options.label: c
options.text: Less dangerous due to low latent heat of evaporation

options.label: d
options.text: More dangerous due to low latent heat of evaporation

expl: Compared to burning in air at 100°C, burning in steam at 100°C is more dangerous due to the high latent heat of vaporisation. The latent heat of a substance is the amount of heat that is absorbed or released by its unit mass during a change of state.

stem: How does a steam engine work?
expl: A steam engine is a type of heat engine, which is used to perform mechanical work using steam (heat). Steam engines are mostly external combustion engines. The Rankine cycle is used in a steam engine. The steam engine was invented by James Watt.

stem: What causes cooling in an air conditioner?
expl: An air-conditioner generally has an air-cooling unit and an air-heating unit. The air-heating unit increases heating when the air temperature falls below a fixed point, and when the temperature becomes higher, the air-cooling unit brings the air to the set level through cooling. The air-cooling unit is a compressor-type mechanical refrigeration unit.

stem: In winter when you touch a log of wood and a rod of iron, you will feel that rod of iron is colder than wood because –

options.label: a
options.text: The heat of rod of iron is less than the heat of log of wood

options.label: b
options.text: In comparison to wood, iron is good conductor of heat

options.label: c
options.text: In comparison to wood, iron is bad conductor of heat

options.label: d
options.text: The rod of iron is heavier than the log of wood

expl: Iron is a good conductor of heat, whereas wood is a poor conductor (insulator). In a cold morning, iron conducts heat away from our hand quickly, so it feels colder than wood. Wood conducts heat slowly, so it feels comparatively less cold.

stem: Heat transfer that does not require a medium is called
expl: In radiation, no medium is required for heat transfer. In solids and liquids, a material medium is required; heat transfer occurs by conduction in solids and by convection in liquids.
